method.rule: Apply chronology before any directional fit. A present-day named sky pattern cannot cause an event older than the relevant stellar population, and J2000 coordinates cannot be back-projected over Myr without source phase-space reconstruction.
method.orion_belt_population_age_envelope_used: few Myr to <10 Myr for the relevant Orion Belt / OB1b environment

site_results.name: Libyan Desert Glass field
site_results.reason: The event predates the present Orion Belt / OB1b stellar population by many millions of years.
site_results.special_context: Later Egyptian royal use of Libyan Desert Glass is archaeologically interesting but cannot retroactively make the 28.5 Ma formation event an Old Kingdom Osiris event.

site_results.name: Nordlinger Ries / moldavite event
site_results.reason: The impact predates the young Orion Belt / OB1b population used by the current hypothesis.

site_results.name: Aouelloul crater
site_results.reason: The event is younger than the broad Orion Belt population age ceiling, but this supplies no causal link.

site_results.name: Tenoumer crater
site_results.event_age: published age uncertain; nominal Meteoritical Bulletin value about 21.4 +/- 9.7 ka

site_results.name: Wabar impact crater field
site_results.local_mechanism: iron meteorite impact into dunes with fused sand and impact glass
site_results.reason: Its young age makes celestial reconstruction tractable but also makes it far too recent to be an origin event for Old Kingdom Osiris/Pyramid Text traditions.

giza_control.rule: Absence of a regional melt/vitrification horizon at Giza is not positive evidence for a failed ancient machine, missing component, wrong coordinate or incomplete attempt.

phallus_spear_overlay.statement: The Osiris phallus may be used as a symbolic analogy to a spear/axis/required component inside JANUS narrative modeling, but no archaeological or physical evidence currently identifies it as a missing technological emitter, key or beam component.

existing_sky_geometry_note.interpretation: In the frozen J2000 coordinate receipt LOVE lies much closer than EDEM to the great-circle extension of the Orion Belt. This is a post-hoc spherical relation, not evidence that either point was targeted by an ancient or natural beam.
